title: Observed human cervical spinal-cord H&E sections
authors: Lukas F. Reissig, Genova Carrero-Rojas, Udo Maierhofer and colleagues
license: CC BY 4.0, source PDF page21 and owning publisher notice; no separate Figure1 exclusion
specimen: Cervical segments C4–C6 from 15 human body donors, five different subjects per postmortem interval group24/48/72h; seven women/eight men, ages58–103, no history of neurological disorders. Exact illustrated age/sex/segment not assigned. Separate39-year-old2h thoracic organ donor is not Figure1a.
preparation: 4%PFA in0.1M phosphate buffer24h at4°C, sucrose cryoprotection, frozen,10µm cryosections, hematoxylin3min/eosin1min, dehydrated and DPX-mounted. Preparation/staining colours, not live tissue.
orientation_scale: pr posterior roots at top-left, ar anterior roots lower-left, deep anterior fissure below supports posterior-up/anterior-down inference. No body side assigned. Caption assigns1000µm bar to a–c, printed at lower-right panelc. No invented calibration.
teaching_scope: Observe full cervical cross-section grey/white relationship and compare postmortem preparation. b/c are different-donor half-sections, not registered stages in a living cord. No cell counts, tract map, central-canal patency or functional signal propagation inferred.
modifications: None: complete source JPEG stream without crop, resampling, enhancement, recolouring, new labels or overlays.
print: Intended110mm≈346ppi. Actual print composition and label/readability review pending.
